title: What is known about 1RB1LA_1LC0RE_1LF1LD_1RE0LC_1LB1RA_---0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_1LC0RE_1LF1LD_1RE0LC_1LB1RA_---0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, probably halting; reduced in Lean to an exact map. The run is a sequence of phases. In a phase, a block of x ones grows to ⌊3x/2⌋+7 while a counter c of copies of 01 counts down by 2. When c runs out the machine halts if x is in one residue class out of four, and otherwise starts a new phase with c about x. The step, the resets and halts_iff (halts iff the orbit of (4, 4, 3) under the map meets a halt) are proved in Lean for all x; phases 0, 1 and 2 are evaluated exactly and do not halt. The end of phase 3, after about 10203 steps, depends on the residue mod 4 of a number with 10101 digits. Heuristically each phase halts with chance 1/4.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 29,502 cells have been visited and 28,395 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The step: S<sub>t</sub>(x, c+2) reaches S<sub>t</sub>(⌊3x/2⌋+7, c)
claims.text: St(x, c) is the head in state A on the first cell of 1^x (01)^2 1^6 (01)^c 1^t 0 1^2, t = 3 or 6. For every x ≥ 1, every c and every rest of the tape: S(x, c+2) reaches S(⌊3x/2⌋+7, c). Each round (a 0 walking through the left block) takes two ones off the left block and adds three to the middle one, W(x+2, b+1) → W(x, b+4); at x = 2 or 1 the middle block becomes the new left block and two copies of 01 rebuild the marker.

claims.title: The reset, as an exact map
claims.text: When c reaches 0 or 1 (the last step ends on the tail 1^t 0 1^2), the middle block becomes a block 1^B behind 1^4 0 or 1^5 0, with B = 3⌊x/2⌋+7 (+t if c = 0). Depending on the parity of B this either halts (state F reads a 0) or is converted, maybe with a short restart, into a new phase: S3(4, (B−5)/2), S3(6, (B−8)/2) or S3(5, (B−5)/2) after c = 0; S6(4, (B−3)/2), S6(6, (B−6)/2) or S6(5, (B−3)/2) after c = 1, t = 3; and after c = 1, t = 6 a short phase that ends at S3(⌊3y/2⌋+4, 1), y = B or B+1. With the step this is a map next on (x, c, t), and St(x, c) leads to next(x, c, t) for every x ≥ 1 and c, by 34 more symbolic rules and induction.

claims.title: Halts iff the orbit of (4, 4, 3) under the map reaches a halt
claims.text: Blank tape reaches S3(4, 4) at step 388, so the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from (4, 4, 3) is a halt.

claims.title: The reset table by residue classes
claims.text: Read off next: from St(x, 2) (one step to c = 0, then the reset) it halts exactly for x ≡ 1, 6 (mod 8) if t = 3 and x ≡ 2, 5 (mod 8) if t = 6; from S3(x, 1) for x ≡ 2 (mod 4); from S6(x, 1) (through the short phase) for x ≡ 0, 9, 11, 14 (mod 16). One class in four each time; otherwise c′ = 9x/8, 3x/4 or 27x/16 plus a constant. The table agrees with next for every x < 3000 and with direct simulation for every x < 200.

claims.title: The run from blank, by simulation
claims.text: Direct simulation: the run reaches S<sub>3</sub>(4, 4) at step 388, S<sub>3</sub>(4, 22) at step 2,684 after a reset at x = 13, and S<sub>3</sub>(6, 1138) at step 6,224,444 after a reset at x = 1007; the first 16 steps of phase 2 follow the step rule exactly (x = 6, 16, 31, 53, 86, …, 8600 at step 9.5·10<sup>7</sup>).

claims.title: No halt in phases 0, 1 and 2
claims.text: The first 585 terms of the orbit of (4, 4, 3) contain no halt: phase 0 from S3(4, 4), phase 1 from S3(4, 22), phase 2 from S3(6, 1138) (568 steps, ending at S3(x, 2) with x ≈ 2.06·10101, x ≡ 7 mod 8), and term 585 is S3(6, c) with c odd and above 10101 (c ≈ 2.3·10101), reached after about 10203 machine steps. Evaluated with exact integers by compiled code; with halts_iff this rules out a halt before phase 3.

claims.title: Phase 3 is out of reach
claims.text: Phase 3 ends at S<sub>3</sub>(y, 1) with y the result of (c−1)/2 applications of x ↦ ⌊3x/2⌋+7 to 6, and halts iff y ≡ 2 (mod 4). y has about 10<sup>101</sup> digits and cannot be computed; no shortcut for its residue is known.

claims.title: Probably halts, after an astronomical time
claims.text: Every reset halts for exactly one residue class in four, and the residue of x after many steps of ⌊3x/2⌋+7 behaves like a random number. So each phase from phase 3 on halts with chance about 1/4, independently, and the machine halts with probability 1 in this model, most likely within a few phases. Each phase is exponentially longer than the one before (c′ is about x, and x grows like 1.5<sup>c</sup>), so a halt, if it comes, comes after a tower of exponentials of steps. This is the «probviously halting» situation: no proof either way is in sight.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Exactly when the orbit of (4, 4, 3) under next reaches a halt (proved). The first chance is the end of phase 3, where the question is whether the ((c−1)/2)-th iterate of x ↦ ⌊3x/2⌋+7 from 6, for a known c ≈ 2.3·10101, is 2 mod 4.

explainer.lede: Probably yes, but nobody can say when or prove it. The machine runs countdowns, each set by the result of the last; when one runs out it halts for one residue class in four. All of this is proved in Lean; the first three countdowns do not halt, and the fourth ends after about 10<sup>203</sup> steps on a number with 10<sup>101</sup> digits.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 29,502 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt, proved in Lean from the exact map; phase 3 starts after about 10<sup>203</sup> steps.
Residue classes of x for which a reset halts, in each of the four kinds of reset, read off the map proved in Lean.
Where phase 3 starts; its end decides the first possible halt.

sections.heading: A countdown that sets the next countdown
html: After a few hundred steps the tape always looks like
the head in state A on the first cell. Call it St(x, c). The run from blank tape reaches S3(4, 4) at step 388.

The head walks a 0 to the right through the block of x ones and comes back: each round takes two ones off the left block and adds three to the middle block 1^6. When the left block is gone, the middle block, now about 3x/2 long, becomes the new left block, and two copies of 01 from the counter are used to rebuild the marker (01)^2 1^6 behind it:
(proved in Lean for every x; it takes about 1.5x2 steps). So within a phase c is a countdown and x grows by a factor of 3/2 per step.

When c reaches 2 or 1 the copies of 01 are used up. The block of x ones is then rewritten into a new block of copies of 01, about 9x/8, 3x/4 or 27x/16 of them, and the machine starts again from St′(4, c′), St′(5, c′) or St′(6, c′); or it halts (state D meets 1 1 0 at the left end, then C and F). Which happens depends only on x modulo 8, 4 or 16, and in each of the four cases exactly one class in four halts (the exact map is proved in Lean; this table is read off it):

Phases 0 and 1 and the start of phase 2 are seen in direct simulation. The end of phase 2 is 568 steps of x ↦ ⌊3x/2⌋+7 later; since the step and the resets are proved for every x, Lean evaluates the whole map through phase 2 and proves that the machine does not halt before phase 3.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.432). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 29,502 cells (22,299 left of the start, 13 right), with a density of 1s of 0.962.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Probviously halting
html: Each reset is a coin with a 1/4 chance of halting, decided by the last few bits of the result of many steps of x ↦ ⌊3x/2⌋+7. Nothing is known that would make those bits predictable, and they look random. So the machine probably halts, most likely at the end of phase 3, 4 or 5, but each phase is exponentially longer than the last, and the first open coin already needs the low bits of a number with 10101 digits. Proving it halts would need a way to compute those bits without the number; proving it does not halt would need a reason why the coins always fall the same way, and there is none.

summary: A countdown phase: x -> floor(3x/2)+7 while c counts down; at the end it halts for one residue class of x in four, else a new countdown of length about x. Step, resets and halts_iff proved in Lean; phases 0-2 do not halt (native); phase 3 is out of reach.
family: nested exponential counter with a residue-class halt (probviously halting)
